questions.question: As per the Hindu calendar, Ugadi festival in southern states of India is celebrated in which of the following months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ugadi**

 
 
• Ugadi, which is observed as Andhra Pradesh's **Hindus' New Year's Day**, is observed on the first day of the Hindu Luni-Solar Calendar in the month of **Chaitra**.
 
• According to the Gregorian calendar, it takes place in either **March or April**.
 
• This Indian holiday **heralds** the arrival of pleasure, joy, hope, and light.
 
• The Sanskrit words "**Yuga**," which means age, and "**adi**," which means the beginning, are combined to form the word "**Ugadi**."
 
• It denotes the start of a new era in** plain terms**.
 
• In Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, this holiday is celebrated with **great zeal and passion**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ninth month of the Hindu calendar is **Agrahya** or Mrga.
 
• The Hindu month of **Vaisakha** corresponds to April or May on the Gregorian calendar. in the national calendar of India.
 
• The fifth month of the Hindu calendar is **shravan**.

questions.question: In September 2022, which legislative assembly withdrew a bill aimed at prohibiting the movement of stray cattle on roads and public places in urban areas of the state, months after it was passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stray Cattle movement**.

 
 
• In **September 2022** **Gujarat **legislative assembly withdrew a bill aimed at prohibiting the movement of **stray cattle** on roads and public places in **urban areas** of the state, months after it was passed.
 
• After returning the** "Gujarat Cattle Control (Keeping and Moving) In Urban Areas Bill" **to the state's **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** administration and asking them to "reconsider it and make necessary revisions," state governor AcharyaA few days later, **Devvrat **retracted the plan..
 
• The bill, which was approved by the Assembly in April of this year, required **cattle-rearers** to seek a licence in order to maintain certain **animals**, such as **stray cows and bulls**, in cities and towns and to have them tagged; if they failed to do so, they risked being imprisoned.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On the first day of the two-day Assembly session, **Minister **of State for Urban Development **Vinod Moradiya** put the bill's withdrawal motion up for a **vote**.
 
• However, after receiving full support from the opposition **Congress**, the **BJP **administration withdrew the request.The opposition **Congress** protested the passage of the law during the last Assembly session on **April 1**, calling it a** "black Act"** while it was being discussed.

questions.question: Who became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of Alivardi Khan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siraj Ud Daulah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__**Siraj Ud Daulah **

 __
 
• **Siraj Ud Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of Alivardi Khan.**
 
• The last independent Nawab of Bengal was **Mirza Muhammad Siraj-ud-Daulah,** also known as Siraj-ud-Daulah[a] or Siraj ud-Daula.
 
• The **East India Company** began to dominate Bengal by the conclusion of his reign and, eventually nearly the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• On **June 23, 1757**, Siraj was betrayed by **Mir Jafar,** the Nawab's army's commander, and lost the **Battle of Plassey.**
 
• The East India Company took over **Bengal's government **after an invasion by its armies, led by **Robert Clive.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Nawab of Bengal in 1756**

 
 
• The **three territories of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa**, which today make up the independent nation of Bangladesh and the Indian states of West Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, were de facto ruled independently by the Nawab of Bengal in the early 18th century.
 
• The Nawabs had their **headquarters in Murshidabad**, which was in the middle of **Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.** The first Nawab was their leader, a former prime minister.

questions.question: An early temple at Bhitargaon, Uttar Pradesh was built about 1500 years ago was made of _______.

__
 
• **Bhitargaon**

 
 
• **​**The greatest** Indian brick temple** to have survived from the **Gupta Empire **is located in **Bhitargaon**, a town close to **Kanpur **in the Kanpur region of **Uttar Pradesh**, India.
 
• Many of the original elements are still present despite the extensive restoration. It dates to the **fifth century**, late.
 
• A **terracotta panel** fronts the terraced brick structure that houses the **Bhitargaon** **Temple**.
 
• It is the earliest surviving brick/terracotta Hindu shrine with a roof and a towering **shikhara**, but its upper chamber did experience significant damage in the **18th century**.
 
• It was constructed in the 5th century during the **Gupta dynasty**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Overlooking the **garbhagriha **is an enormous **pyramidal **spire. Terracotta wall decorations with images of **Shiva**, **Vishnu**, and other **deities** adorn the walls.
 
• When **Alexander Cunningham **first arrived, the porch and the **ardhamandapa**, which eventually fell, were still in tact.

questions.question: Which theory discusses the relationship between ligand bonding and degradation of d orbitals in metal complexes and the geometry of metal complexes and the splitting of d orbitals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Crystal field theory (CFT).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crystal field theory (CFT)**

 
 
• ​**Crystal field theory (CFT) discusses the relationship between ligand binding and degradation of d orbitals in metal complexes, the geometry of metal complexes, and the splitting of d orbitals.**
 
• The **propensity of transition metals **to form complexes is one of their key characteristics. A complex can be thought of as having several ligands encircling a core metal atom or ion.
 
• **Crystal field** **theory** governs how these ligands interact with the central **metal atom or ion.**
 
• The interaction between a **metal ion and ligand** is viewed by the 1929-founded crystal field theory as essentially an electrostatic phenomenon, with the ligands being considered as point charges close to the **atomic orbitals of the central atom.**
 
• Using **molecular orbital theory**, crystal field theory was developed and expanded to consider the partially covalent nature of bonding between the **ligand and metal atom.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **metal-ligand bond** was defined by crystal field theory as an ionic bond that solely results from **electrostatic interactions between the metal ions and ligands.**
 
• In the crystal field theory, anions are viewed as **point charges**, whereas neutral molecules are viewed as dipoles. **Transition metals' d orbitals degenerate**, or have the same energy, when they are not bound to any ligands.
 
• Due to the varied **symmetries of the d orbitals** and the inductive influence of the ligands on the electrons, the d orbitals split apart and become non-degenerate when they begin bonding with other ligands.

 Buddhadeb began his teaching career as an economics instructor at the **University of Burdwan's Shyamsundar College **before moving on to** City College in Calcutta.** He started making films in 1976 after becoming frustrated with the disconnect he saw between the socio-political reality and the economic theory he was teaching.

__
 
• On August 26, 2022,** Dr Samir V. Kamat was named Chairman of the DRDO and Secretary of the Department of Defence R&D.**
 
• **Dr Kamat earned his PhD in Materials Science and Engineering from The Ohio State University, USA, in 1988** after completing his B. Tech. (Hons.) in Metallurgical Engineering at IIT-Kharagpur in 1985. **He joined the DRDO in 1989.**
 
• **Dr Kamat has led and directed a number of crucial material programmes at DRDO,** including the development of high-strength steels for naval ship hulls, high-temperature titanium alloys, and nickel base superalloy based components for aero-engines, the development of tungsten heavy alloys for kinetic energy penetrators, the development of fused silica radomes for missile seekers, and the development of armour solutions for personnel as well as combat vehicles and scout vehicles. These have been used in a number of the systems that the** DRDO laboratories** are creating.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation**

 
 
• ​**The Ministry of Defence of the Government of India's Department of Defence Research and Development,** which has its **main office in Delhi, India, **and is responsible for the research and development of the military, is home to the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO),** the leading organisation in that department.
 
• It was created in 1958 by the **union of the Defence Science Organisation and the Technical Development Establishment and Directorate of Technical Development and Production of the Indian Ordnance Factories.**
 
• The **Defense Research & Development Service (DRDS)** was later established by **the Ministry of Defence in 1979** as a service for Group "A" Officers and Scientists, directly under its administrative jurisdiction.

questions.question: An undifferentiated layer, ______, is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mesoglea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mesoglea is a gelatinous substance** that is **undifferentiated and found in jellyfish and other coelenterates between the outer layer and inner cellular layer.**
 
• **Mesoderm creates the intermediate layer in the early trilaminar embryo germ layers. Triploblastic animals contain it.**
 
• The epiblast cells begin converging at the midline and ingressing at the major streak during gastrulation in both birds and mammals. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coeliac**

 
 
• ​**Coeliac disease, sometimes known as celiac disease in American English,** is a chronic autoimmune condition that **mostly affects the small intestine and causes intolerance to the protein gluten, which is found in grains including wheat, rye, and barley.**
 
• The basic **symptoms of gastrointestinal problems include chronic diarrhoea, abdominal distention, malabsorption, appetite loss, and failure to grow normally in children.**
 
• **This frequently begins between the ages of six months and two years.** Non-classical symptoms are more common, especially in people older than two years.
 
• Any part of the body could be affected by a wide range of symptoms, there can be none at all, or there might be barely perceptible gastrointestinal symptoms.
 
 ​**Acoelomata**

 
 
• **​An animal without a coelom, or formal bodily cavity, is said to be an acoelomate.** Only multicellular organisms with real tissues can develop true body cavities. There are creatures like coral and jellyfish in this class, the eumetazoan, which have just two fundamental tissues. Three different tissue types exist in triploblastic eumetazoan.
 
• The simplest type of animal, an acoelomate has three genuine tissues. In that order from the inside to the outside, these tissues are the endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm. These tissues touch back-to-back with no room in between in an acoelomate. **The mesoderm surrounds the organs as they develop inside of them. **The digestive tract is formed by the endoderm, while the ectoderm makes up the skin.

questions.question: Developing place of settlement is called _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Site**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Site**

 
 
• The location where a structure or settlement grows is referred to** as its site.**
 
• **A site is described as a location where something is built**, or constructed, or as a location where a major or historical event took place.
 
• A site would be the property you purchase and plan to build your new home on.
 
• **The physical qualities of the local terrain are included in the term "site," which refers to the actual location of a colony on Earth. **
 
• **Climate, landforms, water, vegetation, accessibility, soil quality, minerals, and animals are some of the site-specific characteristics.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Settlements**

 
 
• Humans who have established a stable community over an extended period of time in a particular location are considered to **live in settlements**.
 
• A modest fishing town on a river in a distant place can be considered a settlement, as opposed to a metropolis, which is a **sophisticated population hub**.
 
• **Towns, villages, cities, hamlets, bases**, and** camps** are some of the several names for settlements.
 
• Any planned pattern of human living can be categorized as a **settlement**.

questions.question: How many times has India hosted the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup (One Day)?

• **4 times **times has India hosted the** ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup (One Day)**
 
• ​The** One Day International (ODI) Cricket World Cup**, also known as the** ICC Men's Cricket World Cup**, is the sport's global championship.
 
• Every four years, the** International Cricket Council (ICC**), the sport's governing body, hosts the competition, which consists of preliminary qualification stages and a finals **tournament**.
 
• The competition is one of the most watched athletic events in the world, according to the **ICC**, who also refer to it as the** "flagship event of the international cricket calendar."**

• The first men's event was preceded by a **Women's Cricket World Cup**, while a competition with multiple international teams was held as early as **1912 **when **Australia**, **England**, and **South Africa** competed in a **triangular **tournament of** Test matches**.

**Note -**

 
• The **1987** World Cup was jointly hosted by **India** and** Pakistan**, with matches played across both countries.
 
• India co-hosted the** 1996** World Cup with Pakistan and Sri Lanka, and the tournament was played across 22 venues in the three countries.
 
• In 2011 India,Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh Host the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.

questions.question: In India initially, HYVP was implemented in about how much area?

• **HYVP**

• **​**The **High Yielding Variety Programme (HYVP)**, which had as its goal the achievement of food self-sufficiency by** 1970–1971**, was introduced in the Kharif of** 1966–1967**.

questions.question: Which of the following greenhouse gases is most abundant in the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water Vapour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Greenhouse gasses**

 
 
• A **greenhouse gas**, often known as a greenhouse gas **(GHG or GhG)**, is a gas that creates the **greenhouse** **effect** by **absorbing **and **radiating **heat **infrared** light.
 
• **Water vapour **(H2O), **carbon dioxide** (CO2), **methane **(CH4), **nitrous oxide** (N2O), and **ozone** are the planet's main **greenhouse gases **(O3).
 
• Without **greenhouse gases, the average surface temperature of the Earth **would be closer to -**18 °C (0 °F)** than it is today, which is **15 °C (59 °F)**.
 
• **Greenhouse gases** are found in the atmospheres of **Venus**, **Mars**, and **Titan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Water Vapour **

 
 
• **Water vapour**, or aqueous vapour are all terms for the **gaseous** state of **water**.
 
• It is a particular kind of water condition inside the **hydrosphere**.
 
• **Water vapour** can be created by the boiling or evaporation of **liquid water **as well as by the sublimation of ice. 
 
• **Water vapour **is continuously produced by **evaporation **and eliminated by **condensation** in a normal **atmosphere**.
 
• It causes convection currents that can result in clouds since it is less dense than the majority of the other **air constituents**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon dioxide**

 
 
• The **most significant contributor to the warming effect**, accounting for 64% of the total.
 
• Carbon dioxide is long-lived in the atmosphere, with 40% remaining after 100 years, 20% after 1,000 years, and 10% after 10,000 years.
 
 
 
• **Methane**
 
 
• The** second-largest contributor,** accounting for 19% of the total.
 
• Methane is more potent than carbon dioxide, with a global warming impact that's almost 30 times greater over 100 years.
 
 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**
 
 
• The **third-largest contributor,** accounting for 8.1% of the total.
 
• CFCs were widely used in the mid-1900s, but they are still long-lived in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Nitrous oxide**
 
 
• A powerful greenhouse gas with a GWP that's around 270 times that of carbon dioxide.
 
• It remains in the atmosphere for a little more than a century. 
 
 
 
• **Other greenhouse gases include:**
 
 
• Fluorinated gases
 
• Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs)
 
• Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
 
• Perfluorocarbons (PFCs)
 
• Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6)
 
• Nitroge n triflouride (NF3)

questions.question: Who among the following was the best-known Chahamana ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prithviraja III**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prithviraja III**

 
 
• **Prithviraja III** was the best-known **Chahamana **ruler.
 
• From **1177 to 1192 CE**, **Prithviraja III**, sometimes referred to as Prithviraj Chauhan or Rai Pithora, ruled **Sapadalaksha**.
 
• He belonged to the **Chauhan **(Chahamana) dynasty, and his capital was Ajmer in modern-day Rajasthan. In **1177 CE**, when **Prithviraj **ascended the throne as a boy, he inherited a kingdom that ran from **Thanesar **in the **north **to **Jahazpur **(Mewar) in the **south**.
 
• He sought to enlarge this realm by engaging in **military **operations against nearby **countries**, most notably by defeating the **Chandelas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In **1191 AD**, **Prithviraj **oversaw a coalition of **Rajput** princes that routed **Muhammad Ghori's** Ghurid army near **Taraori**.
 
• However, Ghori reappeared with a force of mounted **Turkish** archers in **1192 CE** and overcame the Rajput army there. However, **Prithviraj **was killed in the battlefield and lost the war.
 
• In numerous **semi-legendary texts**, most notably the **Prithviraj Raso**, his defeat at **Tarain **is described as a turning point in the **Islamic **conquest of **India**.

questions.question: In which year was the Indian Parliamentary Group established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1949**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Indian Parliamentary**

 
 
• The** Indian Parliamentary** Group established in **1949**.
 
• ** **The **Parliament **is the supreme **legislative **body of the **Indian Republic** ** Bhratya Sansad.**
 
• The two **houses **that make up India's bicameral legislature are the **Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) (House of the People).
 
• In his capacity as head of the **legislature**, the **president **has full authority to **prorogue **either house of **Parliament **or dissolve the **Lok Sabha.**
 
• The **president **can only use these **powers **if they are recommended by the **prime minister** and his **Union Council of Ministers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Members of **Parliament** are those chosen by voters or proposed by the **president **for a seat in either house **(MPs)**.
 
• The members of the **Rajya Sabha** are chosen by the members of all state legislative assemblies via proportional **representation**, whereas the members of the** Lok Sabha** are chosen by the** Indian population** directly through voting in single-member **districts**.
 
• The **authorised **membership of the **Parliament **is 543 in the **Lok Sabha** and **245 **in the **Rajya Sabha**, including **12 candidates **with experience in a variety of **literary**, **artistic**, **scientific**, and **social service** disciplines.

questions.question: Which of the following revolts was led by Kanhu and Sidhu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santhal Revolt** __

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Santhal Revolt** 

 
 
• **Santhal Revolt** was led by **Kanhu **and **Sidhu**.
 
• The **Santhal revolt**, often referred to as the Sonthal uprising or the **Santhal Hool**, was an uprising by the **Santhal** people in what are now **Jharkhand **and **West Bengal**, **Eastern India**, against the British East India Company** (BEIC)** and the **zamindari **system.
 
• The **East India Company** declared martial law on November **10, 185**5, which lasted until** January 3, 1856**, when it was suspended and the revolt was finally put down by the **Presidency **soldiers.
 
• It began on **June 30, 1855**. The four brothers who made up the insurrection were **Sidhu**, **Kanhu**, **Chand**, and **Bhairav**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The British East India Company's **(BEIC**) revenue system, usury practises, and the **zamindari** system in India's tribal region, then known as the **Bengal Presidency**, were all put a stop to as a result of the **Santhals'** **uprising**.
 
• It was a revolt against the oppression of **colonial rule**, which was upheld by the police, the courts, and the local **zamindars **under the** British East India Company's legal system**. A distorted revenue structure served as the vehicle for this **persecution**.

questions.question: Identify an example of diploblastic animals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coelenterates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coelenterates**.

 
 
• ​The name **"Coelenterata"** refers to the animal **phylum** **Cnidaria**.
 
• They have radial **symmetry** and a very basic tissue structure with just two cell layers **(ectoderm and endoderm)**. Examples include hydrae, **jellyfish**, and **sea anemones**, which are solitary, as well as corals, which are frequently **colonial**.
 
• **Coelenterata** rely on diffusion across the tissue layers rather than a specific **circulatory** system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coelenterates **are all aquatic, primarily marine, creatures. The body **morphology **is **diploblastic**, **radially symmetric**, and lacks a **coelom**.
 
• The **hypostome**, the body's only aperture, is encircled by **sensory **tentacles that are either nematocyst- or **colloblast-equipped** to acquire primarily **planktonic prey**.
 
• The **gastrovascular** cavity, also known as the **coelenteron**, is a large cavity that encircles these tentacles. **Digestion **occurs both within and outside of cells. **Simple diffusion **is used to perform **breathing **and **excretion**. The body is covered in a **network **of **nerves**.
